description: We are Unique team from Tajikistan. We build a tool that turns NASA satellite data (HLS, POWER) into one clear action for farmers, sent in Telegram in Tajik or Russian. We already have a working live demo built with Python/FastAPI, React, Leaflet and Docker. We love space data, agriculture and shipping real products fast. Join us if you want your work to reach real farmers. We are looking for: remote sensing/GIS skills, agronomy knowledge, and a native Tajik speaker to polish farmer texts.
summary: Zamin: turning NASA satellite data into one clear, plain-language action for every farmer in Tajikistan, delivered in Telegram in Tajik or Russian
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Zamin turns NASA Earth observation data into one clear, plain-language action for each field of a farming cooperative, and delivers it to the farmer in Telegram in Tajik or Russian. The farmer replies with a single tap, and the answer appears on the agronomist's map within seconds.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: for each field polygon Zamin searches NASA's CMR STAC API for the freshest Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLSS30/HLSL30, 30 m) scene from the last 90 days with less than 30% cloud cover. It reads only the window over the field and removes cloud, shadow and snow pixels with the Fmask layer. NASA POWER adds 30 days of rainfall and root-zone soil moisture.

2. Analysis: NDVI (vegetation), NDMI (moisture) and a salinity index; the field is split into healthy, weak and problem zones using thresholds for the growing, shoulder and dormant seasons, and compared with its own last three seasons to catch real decline.

3. Decision: a rule engine picks exactly one adaptation step, in priority order: R1 high salinity -> leaching, drainage, salt-tolerant crop; R2 problem zone growing three seasons in a row -> crop rotation; R3 weak growth with enough moisture -> nutrition; R4 weak growth and dry soil -> irrigation; R5 normal -> keep monitoring.

4. Delivery: advice up to 600 characters, no jargon, sent by a Telegram bot; buttons "Understood" / "I have a question" close the loop.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

One agronomist can watch every field of a cooperative instead of finding problems too late. Farmers get one concrete step in their own language on the phone they already use. The rotation and salinity rules address Field Shift directly: adapting crop rotation and protecting soil health as the climate changes.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, NumPy, rasterio (HLS Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs), httpx; aiogram 3 (Telegram bot); React, Vite, Leaflet; Docker, nginx; hosted on Render. Automated test suite; role-based access checked on the server.

CREATIVITY AND CONSIDERATIONS

- Closed loop: satellite -> advice -> farmer's reply back on the map.

- Honest by design: every advice says it is a satellite estimate, not a lab soil test, and the data source (live NASA, cache or demo) is always shown.

- Resilient: if NASA is unreachable it falls back to the last live result, then to demo data.

- Season-aware thresholds: a bare field in winter is not an alarm.

- Limits we state openly: 30 m resolution is noisy for very small plots; salinity from spectral indices is an indication, not a diagnosis; Tajik texts still need native-speaker review.

AI USE

The demo voiceover is AI-generated (Kokoro TTS); the demo recording and editing, the presentation and parts of the deployment code were made with the help of an AI assistant (Claude). The video carries a visible notice.

DEMO ACCESS

No login needed: the link opens the farms map directly as a demo agronomist. To try other roles, click Log out and sign in as farmer +992900000002 or admin +992900000003 (password demo1234). The public demo runs on sample (synthetic) farms; live NASA mode is enabled with an Earthdata token.
